sections.title: Logic puzzles
facts: Pigeonhole: $n + 1$ objects in $n$ boxes put two together; $n(k - 1) + 1$ put $k$ together.
To be sure, plan for the worst case, then add one.
Truth-tellers and liars: assume one case and follow it to a contradiction.

sections.title: Invariants & parity
facts: An invariant never changes: a total, a parity, a remainder, a colour count.
Changing a number by an even amount keeps its parity.
Chessboard colouring: a domino covers one black and one white square.

sections.title: Games & strategy
facts: Work backwards: losing positions only lead to winning ones.
Take $1$ to $k$, last stone wins: the losing piles are multiples of $k + 1$.
A break adds one piece; a knockout match removes one player.

sections.title: Clocks & calendars
facts: Angle at $h{:}m$: $|30h - 5.5m|$; the minute hand gains $5.5^\circ$ a minute.
Weekdays repeat every $7$ days; a year is $52$ weeks plus $1$ day ($2$ in a leap year).
Leap years: divisible by $4$, but century years only if divisible by $400$.

sections.title: Mixed sets
facts: Name the topic before you calculate.
Stuck? Draw it, test the choices, work backwards or estimate.
Difficulty rises through the paper: bank the easy points first.
